title: Respiratory Rate versus Auto-PEEP in Airflow Obstruction
subtitle: Investigate how respiratory rate titration influences expiratory time and trapped gas in obstructive respiratory mechanics

patient.summary: Intubated patient with severe obstructive airway disease receiving volume-controlled ventilation.

prediction.question: When the mandatory respiratory rate is increased from 12 to 24 breaths/min in this patient with severe expiratory resistance, how will auto-PEEP, plateau pressure (Pplat), and end-expiratory flow change?

whatToLookAtHint: Observe the expiratory time interval on the flow-time waveform and note the end-expiratory pressure on an expiratory hold.

reflection.question: In a patient with severe expiratory airflow obstruction, why does increasing the set respiratory rate from 12 to 24 bpm exacerbate auto-PEEP?

options.text: Increasing the respiratory rate shortens the cycle time and curtails available expiratory time (Te), preventing prolonged passive emptying.
Higher respiratory rates stimulate active exhalation via abdominal muscle recruitment.
Inspiratory flow becomes turbulent at higher respiratory rates, increasing inspiratory resistance.
The ventilator automatically increases PEEP to match the higher respiratory frequency.

reflection.explanation: In airflow obstruction, passive exhalation is markedly prolonged due to high resistance and time constants. At RR 12 bpm, cycle time is 5.0 s (Te = 4.2 s). Doubling the rate to 24 bpm cuts total cycle time in half to 2.5 s (Te = 1.7 s). Because the lung needs multiple seconds to empty, cutting expiratory time leaves substantially more trapped gas at the onset of the next breath, causing auto-PEEP and plateau pressure to rise.

evidence.claim: Increasing respiratory rate shortens expiratory time, leading to worsening dynamic hyperinflation and auto-PEEP in patients with airflow limitation.
evidence.source: Laghi F, Goyal A. Auto-PEEP in respiratory failure. Minerva Anestesiol. 2012;78(2):201-215.

evidence.claim: Controlled hypoventilation with lower respiratory rates prevents severe dynamic hyperinflation and hemodynamic compromise in obstructive lung disease.
evidence.source: Tuxen DV. Detrimental effects of positive end-expiratory pressure during controlled mechanical ventilation of patients with severe airflow obstruction. Am Rev Respir Dis. 1989;140(1):5-9.
